title: Task 2: campaignArc.ts read-side lifecycle functions
acceptance_criteria: npm run typecheck && npm run test pass. 6 read-side functions exported from @loreweaver/core/internal; each has a passing unit test.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text:
Code review summary for `53dd87d..e920f5f`:

Assessment: Ready to merge

Critical:
- none

Important:
- none

Minor:
- campaignArc.ts:39-50 — `ArcSummaryRow` and the `arcColumns` object are re-declared privately here, mirroring identical definitions in summary.ts. Both are module-private interfaces so there is no compilation problem, but the duplication means a schema change to arc_summary would require two edits. Low risk given the column set is stable and both files are in the same package, but worth noting for whoever later refactors the summary layer.
- campaignArc.ts:88-107 — `openArcIfMissing` uses a two-statement SELECT-then-INSERT pattern inside a DEFERRED transaction (better-sqlite3 default). For a single-writer SQLite deployment this is fine: WAL mode and SQLite's serialised write lock mean no two writes can interleave on a single DB file, and the partial unique index (`campaign_arc_one_open`) would catch any spurious second open arc with a UNIQUE constraint violation rather than silently creating a duplicate. However, the appendSceneLog precedent (loreweaver-ffn / 2a02791) collapsed the same MAX+INSERT pattern into a single INSERT...SELECT to avoid a theoretically racy window. If concurrency concerns ever arise here, the fix would be the same: move the `COALESCE(MAX(sequence_no),0)+1` computation into a subquery inside the INSERT. For a single-process app this is not a practical bug.
- campaignArc.ts:186-200 — `stampSessionWithOpenArc` does a `getOpenArc` read followed by a separate UPDATE. If called in a context where another write could close the arc between those two statements, the UPDATE would silently succeed but stamp an arc_id that is now closed. The spec designates this as a read-side / atomic-open module, so the write-side caller (Task 3) will need to ensure it either calls this inside a transaction or calls it only when holding an open arc just created by `openArcIfMissing`. Documenting this precondition explicitly in the JSDoc would help the Task 3 implementer.

Follow-up:
- loreweaver-x63.3 (Task 3) should call stampSessionWithOpenArc inside the same transaction as the arc rollover to avoid the read-then-update window noted above.
